title: CLR/94/2015 of Piyush Gupta Vs Sunil Kumar Gupta AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CLR No. 94 of 2015
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for
the revisionist.
Mr. S.K. Jain, Senior Advocate
assisted by Mr. Siddharth Jain, Advocate
for the respondent no.1
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for the
respondent no. 7.
Learned counsel for the revisionist
has emphatically raised the provision of
Sub-Section 4 of Section 6 of the Court
Fees Act, 1870, which contemplates that
whenever the question of proper amount
of the Court Fee payable is raised,
otherwise than under Sub-Section 3, the
Court shall decide such question before
proceeding with any other issue.
Having heard the rival contentions
of learned counsel for both the parties, it
transpires that the Original Suit was
instituted by Mr. Sunil Kumar Gupta for
declaration of ownership of 4/15th share
in the whole property, in question,
whereof a sale deed has been executed by
the defendant nos.1 to 3 in favour of
defendant nos.4 and 5. He claims the
ownership for such share on the basis of
a Will dated 21.01.2003 executed by his
mother in his favour.
It is pertinent to mention that the
plaintiff and Mr. Akhil Kumar were the
real brothers, while defendant nos.1 to 3
is the wife and sons of Late Mr. Akhil
Kumar.
I feel that as per provision of the
Law, he is not required to give the Court
fees, calculated on 1/5th of the total value
of 4/15th share being claimed in the
whole property. The Suit has rightly been
evaluated and no question arises to reject
the plaint under order 7 rule 11 C.P.C.

As regards the provision of Section
6(4) of the Court Fees Act (supra) is
concerned, this is not at all applicable
here because such provision is otherwise
than under Sub-Section (3) of the same
Section, on which, the compliance has
been made by the plaintiff.
This revision is bereft of any merit
and it is hereby dismissed.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 26.11.2015
Nadim
